A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Split-then-Merge (StM) research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative comparisons, component ablations, human and VLLM preference studies, and generated-video examples in Tables 2–4 and the figures.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds LayerFlow comparisons, corruption tests, data-scaling experiments, alternative-segmenter evaluations, and detailed affordance studies.

M1.justification: The Decomposer, CogVideoX-I2V Composer, channel-wise conditioning, foreground augmentations, normalized identity-preservation loss, and basic inference procedure remain unchanged. The recursive multi-object demonstration reuses the Composer; it does not establish a new model component or training algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds handheld-background scenes, logically inconsistent compositions, sequential multi-object insertion, and occlusion and corrupted-input scenarios in Sections 4.4–4.5. Training-source coverage remains the same. Whether the original benchmark changed is unresolved: v2 Section 4.1 says DAVIS-only, while Appendix A1.3 retains v1's DAVIS-plus-Animal-Kingdom description.

E2.justification: v2 adds the closely related layer-aware comparator LayerFlow in foreground-conditioned and background-conditioned variants to quantitative, human/VLM, and visual comparisons (Tables 2–3 and Figure 6). This introduces a substantively relevant comparison family beyond v1's five retained baselines.

E3.justification: New protocols include training on 10K/20K subsets, masking and erosion at 10–75% severity, evaluation with SAM-2 plus Grounding-DINO and SAM-3, and six dedicated affordance criteria. The original quantitative metrics are retained despite renumbering. Statements about matched baseline inference settings are additional documentation, not evidence of changed settings.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained augmentation/identity-loss ablation, v2 investigates data-scale dependence, sensitivity to foreground corruption, dependence on the evaluation segmenter, and individual affordance properties. Sections 4.4–4.6 also add real-world stress cases and explicit occlusion/scale failures, addressing questions not tested in v1.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and preference percentages without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Win/tie/lose reporting already appears in v1; additional comparisons and relative ablation percentages do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Original benchmark, preference, and component-ablation scores are retained, including StM's 84.82/92.88/1.22/16.36/19.81 quantitative results. v2 adds LayerFlow outcomes, reduced-data results, corruption and alternative-segmenter scores, affordance preferences, and qualitative successes and failures. These are additional results, not demonstrated improvements over v1 under unchanged conditions.

T1.justification: Equation 1 replaces v1's written latent-plus-noise expression with explicit diffusion-schedule weighting: sqrt(alpha_bar_t) times the original latent plus sqrt(1-alpha_bar_t) times noise. This is a limited correction to the mathematical specification; task definitions and loss mathematics remain equivalent, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain annotation-free split-and-recompose training, transformation-aware augmentation, identity preservation, StM-50K, and superior compositional fidelity. Mentioning dataset release in v2's abstract promotes a contribution already stated in v1's introduction. The expanded experiments support retained claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: v1 emphasizes textual-alignment tradeoffs and inherited decomposition errors. v2 adds explicit occlusion and scale limitations, proposed scale priors, explanations for corruption robustness, and an architecture-versus-data-scale interpretation. It also reframes text as complementary guidance. The new assertion that the 10K model beats every baseline on M1–M4 overstates Tables 2 and 5.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents temporally consistent augmentation and matched inference steps/guidance scales for cascaded baselines, removes the previously listed AdamW beta3 parameter, and supplies six additional judge prompts. Its abstract explicitly advertises code and data at the existing project page. Most hardware, training budgets, preprocessing, and hyperparameters remain unchanged; resource availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: The cited literature and principal distinction from existing composition methods largely remain intact. v2 adds limited positioning through Table 6's task/evaluation-size comparison and discussion of LayerFlow's conditioned variants. The reference-count reduction consolidates duplicate VideoSwap entries rather than removes a distinct cited work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method explanations, and analysis undergo extensive rewriting even where their substance is retained. v2 reorganizes experimental discussion into additional subsections and rebuilds the appendix with a contents list and numbered subsections. These changes extend beyond the insertion of new experiments.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document from two columns to a single-column layout, redraws the Decomposer diagram, redesigns the metrics table, and merges the original benchmark and ablation tables. It adds stress-test and failure figures, expands comparison panels and preference plots, and introduces several new tables. Retained qualitative examples are also rearranged and annotated.

improvement.justification: The LayerFlow comparisons, targeted affordance assessment, robustness checks, and explicit failures improve support for claims that v1 tested less directly. However, new reporting problems limit the gain: the 10K superiority claim contradicts Tables 2 and 5, DAVIS-only evaluation conflicts with Appendix A1.3, and SAM-3 foreground-identity scores differ without explanation between Tables 4 and 7 (82.22 versus 83.9). The revision provides useful additional evidence, but these inconsistencies prevent a clear substantial improvement in overall rigor.
